ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Burning/stinging pain during micturition with increased urinary frequency for just under one week.  
  • No identifiable trigger or exposure.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Symptoms started ≈ 6–7 days ago and have persisted; noted pink-tinged urine today.  
  • Suprapubic aching pain worse during voiding; no radiation.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: none.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: none.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: none.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: none.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: none.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: none.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: none.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: none.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar urinary episodes reported; no prior ENT-related episodes.
  • No previous ED visits or injection therapy for allergy/anaphylaxis.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergy: Clindamycin (reaction not specified).  
  • Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Mebeverine (IBS) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social context:
  • University student (English major), lives in halls with one flat-mate; family lives nearby.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none reported or observed (lips, tongue, uvula, face all appear normal per history).  
- Airway/breathing: no stridor, no respiratory distress reported.  
- Mental status: alert and oriented throughout call; no dizziness or syncope.  
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: patient alone during teleconsultation.

Assessment:
- No ENT pathology identified. Presentation consistent with uncomplicated cystitis/UTI.  
- Justification: dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic discomfort, microscopic hematuria, absence of fever/flank pain; no ENT or airway symptoms.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Arrange drop-off of mid-stream urine sample for dipstick and culture.  
  • Start empirical oral antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin (3-day course) or Trimethoprim (choice to be finalized once culture results available) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Encourage adequate hydration; use Paracetamol as needed for pain.  
- Safety-net/escalation:
  • Seek medical review if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, worsening hematuria, or symptom persistence beyond one week.  
  • Call practice (or emergency services if severe) for any new breathing difficulty, throat swelling, voice change, or facial/tongue swelling (standard anaphylaxis advice when starting new medication).  
- Follow-up:
  • Practice will contact patient with urine culture results and, if necessary, adjust antibiotics.  
  • Return visit if no improvement next week.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – ENT-focused review (otoscopy, nasal/oral cavity exam, neck palpation) and vitals not obtained.  
  – No documentation of prior anaphylaxis plan or auto-injector availability (not expected but routinely queried in ENT/allergy visits).  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear, minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.

document_quality: adequate
